subject: Non-invasive rolling patch validation + cordon & rollback procedure
messages:
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: maria.galvez@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-10-12T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Non-invasive rolling patch validation + cordon & rollback procedure

Team — looping you in for a short-run plan to patch Acme Payments' private deployment (VPC) next week. Request from Acme: a maintenance approach that minimizes control-plane impact, keeps agreed SLAs, and gives them a clear rollback path for audits. High-level ask:

- Target window: Tue 2026-10-20 02:00–06:00 PT (low traffic).
- Scope: runtime OS updates + Redwood runtime minor patch (x.y.3 -> x.y.6) with model-serving binaries unchanged.
- Constraints: customer has pinned model versions and strict KV cache warming requirements.

I drafted a non-invasive approach in the attached patch_matrix_v3.xlsx but want engineering sign-off on the safety mechanisms: cordon vs drain behavior, prefix/KV cache warming, control-plane TTL changes, and an explicit quick-rollback procedure.

Proposed steps (draft):
1) Preflight snapshot + telemetry baseline (48h).
2) Canary nodes (10% of capacity) in a cordoned subnet, run full acceptance tests + workload replay.
3) Gradual rolling update by host-rail (not AZ-bound) with KV cache pre-warm, 20% increments.
4) Automated health gates (latency P95, error rate, cost per token delta).
5) If gate fails, immediate traffic shift to last-known-good and automated de-pinning of new image (fast rollback).

Please review the attached flow diagram and checklist. Monica — highlight any network-level concerns (transport-zone, MTU, BGP flaps) and whether a cordon-only approach is sufficient vs. full drain. Jordan — share canary metrics and gate thresholds from prior Dedicated rollouts. Karthik — confirm runbook hooks for control-plane failover and KV cache TTLs.

maria — thanks for the heads-up; we'll provide a short compliance attestation post-run. Will keep the window short and provide an immediate post-mortem.

- Vanessa
Principal, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, maria.galvez@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-10-12T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Non-invasive rolling patch validation + cordon & rollback procedure

Thanks Vanessa — quick notes after reading the matrix and diagram. I think the unique network risk here is transport-zone overlap between control-plane and data-plane during cordon. Specific items: 

- Cordon-only (no drain) leaves existing KV TCP sessions open; that helps serving continuity but can mask layering issues (e.g., asymmetric routing once nodes rejoin). Recommend: short-lived connection kill (5s) during each host reattach to force session reestablishment while traffic is still small.
- MTU mismatch risk on patched hosts: include an MTU check in preflight and an automated MTU-rollback step (we've had fragmented tokens previously).
- BGP/Route flaps: ensure route dampening for the patch window and a DoNotAnnounce tag for any node-level route changes.

Operational changes to the draft:
- Add a transport-zone validation step (script included in canary-checklist.md) that verifies control-plane endpoints remain reachable from inside customer VPCs during partial cordon.
- Set KV cache pre-warm TTL to 15m for patched nodes (longer than normal) and ramp down once stable to avoid double-service mismatches.

Attachments referenced: cordon_flow_diagram.png (diagram showing host fence vs full drain), canary-checklist.md (scripts and health-checks).

I can lead the network validation on Tue 2026-10-20 00:00–02:00 PT if that works for the team.

- Monica
Staff SRE (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: maria.galvez@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-10-12T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Non-invasive rolling patch validation + cordon & rollback procedure

Agree with Monica. A few additions from the canary/metrics side: 

- Canary footprint: 2 hosts per region (or 10% capacity floor of 4 hosts) with traffic replay for 60 minutes. Run the full regen + model-serving smoke (no model changes) and synthetic qps ramp up to 2x baseline.
- Health gates (fail-fast thresholds):
  * Latency: P95 <= baseline + 40ms for 10m window.
  * Errors: 5xx spike > 0.5% sustained for 5m => fail.
  * Token delta: upstream token cost increase > 6% => fail.
  * KV warm success: cold-miss rate on patched nodes <= 3% after 15m pre-warm.
- Surge limiter (new): set an ingress throttle for patched nodes so they never exceed 1.2x expected qps during ramp. This prevents sudden user-facing spikes if an edge misroutes.

Rollback quick path (operational):
1) Remove patched nodes from LB + mark images deprecated in the control plane.
2) Re-apply last-good image tag across the cluster (or stop auto-updater and pin).
3) Force a short conv-reset on netflow to rebind sessions (script in canary-checklist.md).
4) If rollback fails after 2 attempts (10 minutes), open incident bridge and escalate to Tier-3.

I'll add the surge limiter and thresholds to the patch_matrix_v3.xlsx and update the canary-checklist.

- Jordan
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: maria.galvez@acme-payments.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Non-invasive rolling patch validation + cordon & rollback procedure

Thanks all — Acme accepts the proposed Tue 2026-10-20 02:00–06:00 PT window contingent on two items: 1) a one-page compliance attestation summarizing rollback steps and audit logs to be provided within 24 hours post-run, and 2) confirmation that the canary will not impact payment authorization latency beyond our SLA (P99 <= 200ms).

We also asked procurement to prepare a temporary SLA exception amendment and have DocuSign ready; cc'd docusign@acme-payments.com. Please confirm the final gate thresholds and the post-run artifact delivery plan.

If the tech leads confirm, we'll proceed.

- Maria Galvez
Head of Infrastructure Ops
Acme Payments
